threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think corner shops are just for snacks, not the best source of fresh bread and locally roasted coffee.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old Elvis songs. He got off with a bow, we all clapped—best ride home in ages.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician playing accordion beside a kebab shop while a whole family danced in the rain—Berlin really feels like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can hop on a tram to a spontaneous open-air techno party in the park. It's a Saturday ritual that feels uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're locals if they still call it the 'Civic Center BART' instead of just 'Civic Center.' That’s a dead giveaway.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus where the driver held the door open for a vendor selling snacks. Only in SF does commuting become a marketplace.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals flock to Park Güell. In reality, we prefer the hidden gardens of secrets just a block away where the real vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they struggle to order a 'café con leche' without looking at their phone.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still take the Overground to get everywhere instead of just walking it. Everyone knows you can’t trip over a local pub or a coffee spot!
Last week on the 35 bus, saw a guy knitting a bright orange scarf while debating the merits of pineapple on pizza with a drunk mate. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling on the street while his dog sat patiently beside him, watching the passersby like a proud parent. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you catch a late-night ski instructor rocking a neon onesie while promoting his pop-up hot chocolate stand. Truly a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they roll their eyes at the tourists snapping pics of the murals while blocking the sidewalk. It's a dance we've mastered.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy arguing with a pigeon over a dropped burrito outside the Muni stop. The bird was surprisingly assertive. Classic Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but miss the hidden art studios in the narrow streets where locals sip coffee and sketch.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them clutching a map, trying to use it while standing in the middle of a busy plaza, completely oblivious to the chaos around them.
